raw_response:
My land is about 10 mu, all flat ground, the same fields my family has farmed for generations here on the plain. My son went to Handan years ago. It is just me and my wife now.

I will do what I always do — winter wheat in autumn, summer maize after the wheat comes off. I have done this rotation my whole life. The wheat goes in around October, the maize right after harvest in June. The land knows this rhythm. I know this rhythm.

For seeds, I will buy whatever the agricultural supply shop in town recommends this year — they usually have a good improved wheat variety, something like Kenong 199 or similar, the kind the village has been using for a few years. For maize I always buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or the newer one they have been pushing. I do not save my own seed for these anymore.

For fertilizer, I apply compound fertilizer as base before planting, then urea when the wheat is jointing. I put a good amount — I do not want to see yellow leaves. My neighbor applies the same. For maize I do the same, base fertilizer then chase it with urea at the big bell stage.

Irrigation — wheat needs water four times: before winter, green-up, jointing, and grain fill. The well is still working. For maize it depends on rain, but usually I pump once or twice. Water is more trouble now than before, the pump has to work harder, but I manage.

I also keep half a mu near the house for garlic and vegetables, just for us to eat.
